Root mathematical check: under the usual based homotopy exact sequence for connected fibre, total and base, a zero boundary from Pi2(base) to Pi1(fibre) gives an injective fibre map, and connectedness of the fibre gives a surjective map to Pi1(base). The short exact sequence therefore follows conditionally; the geometric fibration hypothesis itself has not been established here.

Root mathematical check: vanishing of higher homotopy groups of fibre and base forces that of the total space by exactness. This uses the proposed homotopy-fibration interpretation and does not prove a topos or profinite generalisation.

Root counterexample to the final written starred equivalence: a point Y in an open two-dimensional disk X has an unstarred disk neighbourhood, while its punctured neighbourhood is homotopy equivalent to a circle. The three pieces meet the stated asphericity assumptions, and Pi2(Y)=0, but the starred neighbourhood has fundamental group Z while Y has trivial fundamental group. Thus the starred equivalence cannot hold as a general ordinary topological statement; the unstarred target is the refined candidate, consistent with earlier notation. The plainly written star remains in the transcription. The standard homotopy groups of the circle were carried as background, not newly proved.

check_events.outcome: Conditional on the usual based homotopy exact sequence for connected fibre F, total E and base B: exactness gives ker(pi_1(F)->pi_1(E))=im(pi_2(B)->pi_1(F)). The sufficient condition pi_2(B)=0 also makes the boundary zero. This checks the source opening and diagram14 algebraically under its proposed fibration, not the existence of that fibration.
